items: **Harsha Era:** begins 606 AD; associated with Harshavardhana; begins with Harsha's accession.
**Capital shift:** Thaneshwar → Kannauj, by Harshavardhana; Thanesar is the earlier link of Kannauj as Harsha's capital.
**Shiladitya:** alternative title/name of Harshavardhana; he is called Shiladitya.
**Contribution:** patron of Buddhism, literature and learning; Nalanda.

parts.t: Kannauj assembly, Mahamoksha Council and Pulakesin II
items: **Harsha and Kannauj:** religious assembly at Kannauj.
**Kannauj Assembly, attendees:** rulers of 20 countries + Brahmins + Shramanas + courtiers.
**Harsha and Pulakesin II:** Harsha was defeated on the Narmada.
**Source for Harsha-Pulakesin II:** Aihole Inscription + Hiuen Tsang.
**Banabhatta:** court poet of Harsha; Sanskrit scholar / poet; he wrote **Harshacharita** and **Kadambari**.
**Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang / Hieun Tsang):** Chinese Buddhist monk/pilgrim; the Chinese traveller who visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana.
**Religion-related association:** Hiuen-Tsang, in Harsha's period: Mahayana Buddhism + Nalanda.
**Places linked with Hiuen-Tsang:** Nalanda, Sarnath, Bodh Gaya, Kushinagar, Mathura.

parts.t: Kanauj after Harsha and the Tripartite Struggle
items: **Post-Harsha Kanauj:** centre of attraction for competing powers.
**Mahodaya Shri:** old name of Kannauj, associated with Mihir Bhoj.
**Nagar Mahoday Shri:** a sobriquet/title of Kannauj; not its ancient/original name.
**Yashovarman of Kannauj:** his court poet was **Bhavabhuti**, Sanskrit poet; works: Mahaviracharitam, Malatimadhava, Uttararamacharitam.
**Founder:** Nagabhata I founded the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty; **Vatsaraja** is given as the actual founder of the Pratiharas.
**Capitals:** first capital Ujjain; later capital Kannauj.
**Chronology:** Vatsaraja → Nagabhata II → Mahendrapala I → Mahipala.
**Destroyed army of:** a Mlechcha ruler; interpreted in source as probably the Arab ruler of Sindh.
**Rajasekhara (Rajshekhara):** court scholar of the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Mahendrapala-I & Mahipala-I; works: **Karpuramanjari**, Kavyamimamsa, Viddhasalabhanjika.
**Dharmapala's title:** Param Saugat; it indicates Buddhist affiliation.

lectures.title: Badami Chalukyas: rulers and political history

items: **Period:** c. 543–753 CE; Chalukya, 6th–8th CE; key association Vesara.
**Region:** Chalukya rule was mainly Deccan/Southern India, not North India; Badami was the capital.
**Place → dynasty:** Badami/Vatapi → Chalukyas; Kanchi → Pallavas; Tanjore → Cholas.
**Hariti:** Mother Goddess worshipped by the early Chalukyas.
**Founder:** Pulakesin I (Pulakesi-I / Pulakeshi-I / Pulakeshin I) founded the Badami (Vatapi) Chalukya dynasty; he is also described as the real founder.
**Pulakeshin I:** c. 543–566 CE; Ashvamedha associated with him.
**Badami Rock Inscription:** ruler Pulakeshin I; date Saka 465.
**Kirtivarman I:** c. 566–598 CE; annexed Kadambas, Gangas and Mauryas of Konkan.
**Mangalesha:** important ruler between Kirtivarman I and Pulakeshin II.
Pulakeshin II is known as Parameshvara
**Pulakeshin II and Harsha:** defeated/stopped Harshavardhana on the Narmada; Harsha's southward expansion stopped at the Narmada.
**Persia:** received the Persian embassy of Khusrau II around 626 CE.
**Pallava:** Pallava king Narasimhavarman I captured/destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and assumed the title Vatapikonda.
**Most important enemy pairs:** Pulakeshin II ↔ Harsha; Narasimhavarman I ↔ Pulakeshin II.
**Marturu inscription:** issued by Pulakesin II; refers to Mangalagiri as Mangalapura.
Pulakeshin II; key source for Pulakeshin II
Aihole, Karnataka; preserved at Meguti Jain Temple
**Mentions Kalidasa and also Bharavi:** because Ravikirti compared his fame with theirs.
**Lohnara Inscription:** ruler Pulakeshin II; date 630 AD; Harsha is NOT mentioned among the defeated enemies.

parts.t: Later rulers and the end of the dynasty
items: **Vikramaditya I:** c. 655–680 CE; restored Chalukya power after the Pallava invasion.
**Vikramaditya I, new inscription:** 7th-century inscription discovered at Madapura Lake, Davangere; concerns land-grant practices.
**Vikramaditya II:** c. 733–746 CE; defeated the Pallavas three times and captured Kanchi.
**Last ruler:** Kirtivarman II, c. 746–753 CE; overthrown by Rashtrakuta Dantidurga.

lectures.title: Badami Chalukyas: women, architecture and travellers

items: **Women in administration:** the Chalukyas frequently gave high-ranking administrative positions to women.
**Vijaya Bhattarika:** queen of Chandraditya; issued two copper plates in her own name; poetess; administered the kingdom after her husband's death.
**Kumkumdevi:** sister of Vijayaditya; her recommendation led to the grant of a village to a Jain monastery.
**Core hook:** Badami = rock-cut caves; Aihole = experimental/early temple architecture; Pattadakal = synthesis of Nagara + Dravida.
**Badami Caves:** 4 rock-cut temples; Caves 1–3 Hindu, Cave 4 Jain.
**Lad Khan Temple, Aihole:** one of the earliest temples.
**Pattadakal:** Chalukya architectural centre; Chalukyan architecture; Nagara + Dravida styles represented.
**Vesara:** hybrid of Nagara + Dravida; associated with the Chalukya style.
**Navabrahma (9-temple complex):** at Alampur / Alampuram; Badami Chalukyas.
**Ma-Twa-Lin / Matwalin:** Chinese traveller associated with the account of China–India relations during Chalukya rule.
**Founder:** Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakeshin II.
**Core region:** Vengi region of present-day Andhra Pradesh.
**Capital:** Vengi → later Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) became an important centre.
**Region map:** Badami → Karnataka; Vengi → Andhra Pradesh.
**Political position:** the Eastern Chalukyas became an important power in Andhra–Deccan politics.
**Faith:** the Chalukya rulers of Eastern Vengi are given as followers of Vaishnavism.
**Telugu:** official language under the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.
**Vijayaditya II:** built 108 Saiva / Narendraeswara temples; fought 108 fierce battles over 12 years against the Rashtrakutas (under Govinda III & Amoghavarsha I) and their Gangavadi allies.
**Gunaga / Gunga Vijayaditya:** title Tripura-Martya-Maheswara (victory over Nellore, Kiranapura, Achalapura).
**Last king of the Eastern Chalukyas:** Vijayaditya VII.

parts.t: Temples and the city of Rajahmundry
items: **Bhimeshwara Temple (Godavari banks):** Chalukya Bhima I built the dual twin temples Draksharama Bhimeswara and Kumararama (Samalkota) Bhimeswara.
**Rajahmundry:** established by Ammaraja Vishnuvardhana on the banks of the Godavari as the Eastern Chalukyan capital.
**Rajamahendra (present Rajahmundry):** built during the reign of the Eastern Chalukyas.
**Rajaraja Narendra:** major Eastern Chalukya ruler; associated with Rajamahendravaram.
**Literary landmark:** Nannaya (Nannayya / Nannayabhattu) was patronised by Rajaraja Narendra; he was his court poet.
**Nannaya:** first poet to translate the Mahabharata into Telugu; began the Telugu Mahabharata (Andhra Mahabharatam) translation; Kavi Traya.
**Nandampudi village:** received by Narayana Bhattu from Rajaraja Narendra.
**Telugu literature:** the Eastern Chalukya period is an important phase in the development of the Telugu literary tradition.
**Literature linkage:** Rajaraja Narendra → Nannaya → Telugu Mahabharata.
**Major rivalry:** repeated political interaction/conflict with the Cholas.
**Chola connection:** Rajaraja Narendra of the Eastern Chalukyas was connected with the Chola royal family through marriage.
**Chalukya–Chola link:** Eastern Chalukya succession became increasingly intertwined with the Chola dynasty.
**Kulottunga I:** Rajendra Chalukya / Kulottunga I emerged from the Eastern Chalukya–Chola line and united the two political traditions.
**Traveller:** Matwalin → account of China–India relations during Chalukya rule.
**Foundation:** Dantidurga established the Rashtrakuta dynasty/Empire in 753 AD.

parts.t: Govinda III and the Kannauj struggle
items: **Kannauj struggle:** the Rashtrakutas participated in the Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj.
**Govind III:** defeated Gurjara-Pratihara Nagabhata II during his North Indian campaign.
**Sanjan + Radhanpur** → Govinda III → Nagabhata II defeated.
**Birth:** Amoghavarsha I was born in 800 AD, at Shribhavan, on/near the Narmada, in a military camp.
**Faith:** Amoghavarsha I followed Jainism; disciple of Jain Acharya Jinasena.
**Religion:** Rashtrakuta rulers patronized Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta traditions but showed an inclination toward Jainism.
**Kailasa Temple, Ellora:** built by Krishna I (Rashtrakuta).
Designed to recall Mount Kailasa, abode of Shiva
**Ellora Caves:** Maharashtra; Buddhist + Hindu + Jain rock-cut caves coexist; Rashtrakutas; 34 caves; Kailasa temple (Kailasanatha Temple).
**Elephanta Caves:** Maharashtra; Shaiva / Hindu; given as built by the Rashtrakutas; Trimurti Shiva.
**Decline/successor link:** the Rashtrakutas were eventually overthrown by the Kalyani Chalukyas under Tailapa II (973 CE).
**Architecture, theme:** Dravida influences + Deccan innovation → Kalyani Chalukya style.
**Architecture, features:** ornate pillars; stepped superstructures; decorated doorways; intricate wall motifs; balanced proportions.
**Sculpture:** deities, dancers, musicians, mythical figures, floral/geometric motifs.
**Sculptural style:** increasing ornamentation + dynamism + fine detailing.
**Hoysala link:** the Kalyani Chalukya sculpture/architecture tradition was the precursor to the Hoysala tradition.
